primary_source.paper: Tran et al., f-Differential Privacy Filters: Validity and Approximate Solutions
primary_source.main_validity_scope: Approximate GDP guarantee with asymptotic error under the paper's q-to-zero or q-to-one scaling assumptions; finite q=0.1 Figure 12 is numerical validation, not an exact GDP certificate.
primary_source.source_clarification: Appendix G.2 writes y_i^2 without clarifying scalar output versus vector shorthand, while the main algorithm permits vector outputs. The independent vector sweep cannot establish an omitted-parameter gap because it also used the wrong budget formula; author code/output convention remain unverified.

independent_simulation.classification: exploratory independent source-matched scalar simulation; not author code
independent_simulation.interpretation: Close to the paper's Figure 12 reported halt rates 0.9886/0.9880 and mean 113.1 steps. This supports reproduction of the numerical example, not a novel privacy result.

superseded_sweep.status: hypothetical vector-output exact-KL extension; not a paper reproduction or reporting-gap finding
superseded_sweep.why: The paper's y_i^2 notation does not settle output dimension, and it explicitly uses a different approximate budget.

valid_fully_adaptive_baselines.name: Feldman and Zrnic fixed-order RDP filter
valid_fully_adaptive_baselines.basis: Theorem 4.3: continue iff sum of conditionally valid per-step RDP costs at fixed order alpha stays within B; otherwise halt before release.
valid_fully_adaptive_baselines.implementation_status: local conservative reference wrapper implemented in src/research_platform/rdp_filter_reference.py and unit-tested; no production library validated; revealed-coin per-step charge may be much looser than an optimal subsampled-Gaussian RDP bound

valid_fully_adaptive_baselines.name: Whitehouse et al. fully adaptive (epsilon,delta)-DP / approximate zCDP filters
valid_fully_adaptive_baselines.basis: Explicit fully adaptive filter constructions rather than fixed-schedule accountant composition.
valid_fully_adaptive_baselines.implementation_status: literature baseline only; no local implementation yet pinned

comparison_cautions: The source paper's Figure 12 compares with an order-one RDP-to-(epsilon,delta) conversion at the same B; a multi-order RDP filter is a different information-budget comparison and must be labeled as such.
Ordinary fixed-schedule PLD/RDP composition code must not be presented as a valid fully adaptive filter without a theorem and matching stopping rule.
No linked author simulation code or deployed production accountant has been verified in this audit.

local_valid_baseline_reference.one_step_bound: For alpha>1 and r=mu/sigma, both RDP directions are at most log(1-q+q*exp((alpha-1)*alpha*r^2/2))/(alpha-1), by revealing the Bernoulli subsampling coin and postprocessing.
local_valid_baseline_reference.stop_rule: Before releasing the next mechanism, halt if pathwise sum of frozen-order upper charges would exceed its RDP budget.
local_valid_baseline_reference.limitation: The math bound is valid, but the ordinary floating-point implementation is not a certified numerical accountant. No production or matched-(epsilon,delta) privacy comparison is claimed.

boundary_diagnostic.decision: All three higher-q contrasts meet the preregistered >0.01 discrepancy-increase rule after simultaneous DKW uncertainty; q=0.19 narrowly. The stop probability remains near 0.99 across the sweep, so stopping frequency is not an accuracy diagnostic in this model.
boundary_diagnostic.limitation: This confirms a known finite-q approximation limitation in an independent one-dimensional implementation. No theorem counterexample, formal guard cutoff, or production undercount is established.

remaining_work: Pin or implement a tighter proven subsampled-Gaussian per-step RDP upper bound if comparing utility; the revealed-coin bound is deliberately conservative.
Specify a matched adjacency and (epsilon,delta) guarantee with certified finite-q errors before an operational filter comparison or safety claim.
research_decision: Do not claim an accountant undercount, theorem counterexample, novelty, or production vulnerability. Keep finding 158 as a bounded implementation-audit lead.
